title: Superlinear Wire Lower Bounds Toward P Versus NP
content: The satisfying inputs of a Boolean circuit with \(s\) inputs and wires in all can be counted in time \(2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\) when every gate is either an arbitrary function of at most \(s^{4/5}\) inputs or a threshold, exact, modular or symmetric gate of any fan-in with weights of at most \(s^{2/3}\) bits. Consequently a language in \(\mathrm{ENP}\) needs more than \(cN\sqrt{\log N}\) wires in circuits on \(N\) inputs built from such gates, with arbitrary gates of at most \(N^{3/4}\) inputs and weights of at most \(N^{1/2}\) bits. The \(\mathrm{P}\) versus \(\mathrm{NP}\) problem remains open; we survey where these bounds stand within it.
